# Almide

> The programming language LLMs can write most accurately. Pure-Rust
> compiler, `.almd` source files, dual-target codegen (Rust, WASM).
> Every design decision serves one metric: **modification survival rate**
> on the [almide-dojo](https://github.com/almide/almide-dojo) MSR benchmark.

If you are an LLM writing Almide code, read this file first. It is
concise on purpose. Follow the link map for depth.

## Fast facts

- Extension: `.almd`. Auto-imported (no `import` needed): `string`, `int`,
  `float`, `list`, `map`, `set`, `option`, `result`, `value`, `error`,
  `math`, `datetime`.
  Sized-numeric conversion modules (`int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`,
  `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`, `uint64`, `float32`, `float64`) are also
  auto-imported for UFCS — e.g. `x.to_int64()` on `x: Int32` resolves to
  `int32.to_int64(x)`.
  Everything else needs an explicit `import`: `args`, `base64`, `bytes`,
  `env`, `fs`, `hash`, `hex`, `html`, `http`, `io`, `json`, `matrix`, `mem`,
  `net`, `path`, `process`, `random`, `regex`, `testing`, `zlib`.
- Null is spelled `T?` (shorthand for `Option[T]`, valid in every type
  position — the canonical spelling, `almide fmt` normalizes to it; ADR-0010).
  `?` binds to the preceding type atom, never across `->`: `(A) -> B?` is a fn
  returning `Option[B]`, an optional fn value spells `((A) -> B)?`, nested
  Option spells `(T?)?`. Errors are spelled `Result[T, E]`, or `-> T!` for the
  pure-fallible `Result[T, String]` return (value tails lift into ok(...)).
  A lambda whose body uses `!` is a fallible closure `(A) -> Result[T, String]`
  — first-class, and as a core list-HOF callback it takes the first-err form;
  fn-type slots spell it `(A) -> B!`. In test blocks lambda-`!` stays unwrap. No `null`, no `throw`, no
  exceptions.
- Effectful functions are written `effect fn f() -> T`. Pure functions
  cannot call effect functions (checked, emits E006).
- Generics use `[T]` (not `<T>`). Variants use leading `|`.
- `match` is exhaustive; missing arms emit a warning.
- Multiple lets chain by newline (no `in`). No `let rec`, no `head :: tail`
  cons, no `[a, ...rest]` spread in list patterns.

## CLI

```
almide check <file>          # type-check only
almide run <file>            # compile + execute
almide build <file> -o app   # build binary (default: Rust target)
almide build <file> --target wasm
almide test [pattern]        # run tests (*.almd with `test { }` blocks)
almide fmt <file>            # format
almide compile [module]      # emit .almdi module interface
almide explain E001          # expand a diagnostic code
almide ide outline <file>                 # one-line-per-decl summary
almide ide outline @stdlib/string         # stdlib API listing
almide ide doc string.to_upper            # signature + doc for a symbol
almide ide stdlib-snapshot [--json]       # concatenated stdlib outlines for
                                          # SYSTEM_PROMPT injection (~3.5K tokens)
almide mcp                   # MCP server on stdio: check / test / api / explain /
                             # fmt-check as typed tools with JSON results
```

Machine-readable output (prefer these when a program, not a person, reads it):
`check --json` (one diagnostic per line: `{level, code, message, hint, try,
try_replace, file, line, col}`), `test --json`, `fmt --check --json`,
`compile --json`, `ide outline --json`, `ide stdlib-snapshot --json`.
An MCP client (Claude Code, …) gets the same answers as tool calls via
`almide mcp` — see [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md).

## Core idioms

### Prefer match over if-chains

```almide
// ✗
if kind == "int" then "i64"
else if kind == "float" then "f64"
else "unknown"

// ✓
match kind {
  "int"   => "i64",
  "float" => "f64",
  _       => "unknown",
}
```

### Prefer list combinators over `var + for`

```almide
// ✗
var result: List[String] = []
for item in items { result = result + [transform(item)] }
result

// ✓
items |> list.map(transform)
```

### Recursion for stateful loops (no head :: tail)

```almide
fn skip_ws(s: String, p: Int) -> Int =
  if p < string.len(s) and is_ws(peek(s, p)) then skip_ws(s, p + 1)
  else p
```

For head/tail on lists, use `list.first` / `list.drop(xs, 1)`:

```almide
match xs {
  [] => base,
  _  => {
    let h = list.first(xs)!
    let t = list.drop(xs, 1)
    // ...
  },
}
```

### Effect fn with `guard else err(...)`

```almide
effect fn open_file(path: String) -> Result[String, String] = {
  guard fs.is_file(path) else err("not a file: ${path}")
  fs.read_text(path)!
}
```

### `??` / `?` / `!`

```almide
option.get(v, key) ?? default        // Option fallback
result.get(v, key)?                  // Result → Option (inside a fn returning Option)
parse_int(s)!                        // unwrap a Result, propagate err (effect fn only)
```

### Which error type — a layer, not a taste call

`E = String` is the **erasure** layer: the *reporting* channel, read by humans
and models. It is the DEFAULT and what the whole stdlib uses. A variant `E` is
the **refinement** layer: the *branching* channel, where the program changes
behaviour on the content. Pick it only when you want to branch on the content
AND the domain is closed — a module or package that takes care of that error
itself. Leaving that domain, demote to String; the demotion is always spelled
as a `map_err`, because there is no conversion hook to hide it.

```almide
// erasure (default) — add context, never replace silently
fs.read_text(p) |> result.map_err((e) => "loading config: ${e}")!

// refinement — inside the module that handles these kinds
type LoadError = | NotFound(String) | BadValue(String)

// demotion at the boundary — visible, never implicit
load(p) |> result.map_err((e) => "${e}")
```

Do not branch on message TEXT (`string.contains(e, …)`, `e == "..."`) — E035.
Non-goals, decided and not open: no `From`-style conversion hook, no error
sets / unions / rows, no implicit propagation, no inferred lambda error type,
`main` stays String. Full rule: `docs/specs/result-option-effect.md` §8.0, §9.

### Operators, not comparison functions

Almide uses operators for comparison and equality. There is no
`int.gt`, `int.lt`, `int.eq`, etc. Use `>`, `<`, `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`.
Equality (`==` / `!=`) works on any type.

### sqrt, abs, etc.

`int.sqrt` does not exist. Convert, sqrt, optionally convert back:

```almide
let root_f = float.sqrt(int.to_float(n))
let root_i = float.to_int(root_f)    // truncating
```

`int.abs`, `float.abs` do exist.

## Diagnostic codes LLMs hit most (retry anchors)

| Code | Meaning | Usual fix (from `try:` snippet) |
|---|---|---|
| E001 | Type mismatch | Often Unit-leak: add a trailing expression, or rebind via `let new_x = if cond then … else …` |
| E002 | Undefined function | Often a cross-language idiom (`length` → `len`, `push` → `+ [x]`). Check `almide ide outline @stdlib/<m>` |
| E003 | Undefined variable | Missing explicit `import json` / `import fs` / etc |
| E004 | Arg count mismatch | Signature placeholder in try: shows `<name: Type>` |
| E005 | Arg type mismatch | Often needs explicit conversion (`int.to_string(n)` etc) |
| E006 | Pure fn calls effect fn | Mark the caller `effect fn` |
| E007/E008 | Fan block misuse | See `docs/specs/fan.md` |
| E009 | Reassign immutable | `let` → `var` |
| E010 | Non-exhaustive match | Add the missing arm(s) or `_ => ...` |
| E011 | Mutable var mutated inside closure in pure fn | Refactor with `list.fold` / `list.count` / etc, or mark fn `effect fn` |
| E012 | Duplicate definition (fn / test) | Rename one side |
| E013 | Field access on non-record / missing field | Check spelling; non-records don't have method syntax (see E002) |
| E014 | Unreachable match arm | Drop the dead arm, or tighten the earlier arm so this one is reachable |
| E015 | Possible stdlib reimplementation (warning) | Delegate via the `try:` shim, or rename if intentionally different |
| E016 | Function in a `Set` element or `Map` key | Keep closures in a `List`, or use a comparable key (closures are fine as `Map` values) |
| E017 | Record construction on an enum type name | Construct a specific record-bearing case (`Named { ... }`), not the enum type |
| E018 | Empty collection with an uninferable element type | Annotate the element type (`let xs: List[Int] = []`), or inline (`list.len([]: List[Int])`) — never silently defaulted (Rust/Swift rule) |
| E019 | Ambiguous variant constructor (same ctor name in two or more types) | Rename the constructor in one of the types so the name is unique (a qualified `Type.Ctor` is not yet supported) |
| E020 | Two distinct types share one name with different structures | Rename one of the colliding types |
| E021 | Invalid record construction/pattern shape (positional args on a record, unknown/duplicate/missing field, paren pattern on a record case) | Records take named fields: `Cfg(name: x)` or `Cfg { name: x }`; match record cases as `Case { .. }` |
| E022 | `!` (unwrap-propagate) outside an effect fn body or test block | Mark the enclosing fn `effect fn`, or use `??` for a fallback value (`!` inside a lambda can't propagate) |
| E023 | Derived `Codec`/`Ord`/`Hash` not satisfied by a field type | Add `: P` to the offending field type (every field of a `: P` type must itself be `P`) — or hand-write `Type.encode`/`decode` for Codec |
| E024 | Integer literal out of range for its type (would silently fold to 0) | Use a literal within the type's range. Two causes, two fixes: **magnitude** → smaller literal or wider type (`UInt64` reaches its full `18446744073709551615`); **sign** (`let k: UInt64 = -5`) → drop the `-` or use the signed type of the same width. `-9223372036854775808` (i64::MIN) and `-0` in an unsigned type are both valid |
| E025 | Cannot infer a concrete type — an undecidable type slot (e.g. the error type of a value that is always `ok(...)`) was never pinned | Annotate the binding with its full type (`let r: Result[Int, String] = ...`); an unconstrained slot is an error even if never constructed, never silently defaulted |
| E026 | `[]` indexing on a String (a UTF-8 codepoint sequence, not a byte/char array) | Use `string.get(s, i)` (returns `Option[String]`) or `string.char_at(s, i)`; range slicing `s[a..b]` is fine |
| E028 | `main()` takes no parameters (`fn main(args: List[String])` is not wired on any target) | Read program arguments with `env.args()` inside the body |
| E029 | Unknown type name in an annotation or record literal (would fail the native build after check accepted) | Declare the type, fix the spelling, or add the missing import |
| E030 | Type has no ordering — `list.sort/min/max` or a `sort_by` key over Map/Set/Fn or compound-nested Float | Sort by an explicit orderable key (`list.sort_by(xs, (m) => <Int/String key>)`) |
| E031 | Retired range spelling — `..`/`..=` were replaced by Swift-style `..<` (exclusive) / `...` (inclusive) | Write `0 ..< n` / `1 ... n`, or run `almide fix <file>` to migrate every range mechanically |
| E032 | Immutable binding (or a temporary) passed to a `mut` parameter | Declare the root binding with `var` instead of `let`; a temporary must be bound first (split from E007 in 2026-08) |
| E033 | Opaque type constructed outside its defining module | Use the defining module's public constructor API (split from E008 in 2026-08) |
| E034 | Error-channel operator (`!` / `?` / `??`) on a non-Option/Result operand | Drop the operator — a plain value has no error channel; if a fallible call was intended, apply it to that call's Result |
| E035 | (warning) Branch condition reads error message text (`string.contains(e, …)` / `e == "…"` on an err binding) | Branch on a variant error type or use `??` for a kind-independent fallback; message text is a report, not an API |
| E036 | (warning) `map_err` lambda never uses its error value — original error silently discarded | Keep the chain: `(e) => "context: ${e}"`; discard deliberately with `(_) => …` |
| E037 | Equality between incompatible types (Result on one side only, or same container with different params — used to die as rustc E0308 after check passed) | Unwrap the Result side (`!` / `??` / match), or make both operand types identical |
| E038 | `??` separated from its fallback (line-crossing swallowed the next statement; also the missing-operand form) | Put the fallback on the same line as `??`; multiline = parens with `??` trailing |
| E039 | Retired `result.collect`/`collect_map` — Rust's collect short-circuits, almide's collected ALL errors (opposite strategy, same name); the fns are REMOVED (an ordinary E002 now) | All-errors: `let (oks, errs) = result.partition(rs)` then branch on `list.is_empty(errs)`; first-err: `list.map(xs, (x) => f(x)!)!` |
| E041 | Implicit propagation (auto-?) was REMOVED (ADR-0008) — the value stays a Result in all 5 former positions | Append `!` to propagate (mechanical insertion carried by the error), or consume the Result (`??` / `?` / match) |
| E042 | A statement-position Result is discarded — the error would be silently dropped (must-use, every fn kind) | Propagate with `expr!`, or discard on purpose with `let _ = expr` |
| E043 | `list.try_*` was REMOVED (ADR-0006) — the core HOF is fallibility-polymorphic: a callback ending in `!` (or a named `-> T!` fn) instantiates the fallible form, first-err short-circuit included | `list.try_map(xs, f)` → `list.map(xs, (x) => f(x)!)!` (same shape for filter/flat_map/filter_map/fold/find/each) |
| E044 | a PURE `main` returns Unit — a program's result is its output, not a return value (`fn main() -> Int` used to die downstream as invalid Rust); an EFFECT main may declare any Ok type (its wrapper discards the payload) | `fn main() -> Unit = println("${...}")`, or `process.exit(n)` for an exit code |
| E045 | tuple index `.k` is defined only on tuples and only below the arity — `.0` on Int, or `.5` on a pair, is a check-time error naming the type/valid range (previously an Unknown that died at build as a compiler-blaming banner, #1266) | index within `.0`..`.arity-1`, or destructure: `let (x, y) = t` |
| E046 | `_` in a call ARGUMENT is not a value and is NOT partial application — it lowered to `Unit` and died at build as a compiler-blaming banner (`add(_, 10)` → `add((), 10i64)`); measured: binding it typed the RETURN type, and in pipe position it counts as an extra argument (E004). `_` in EXPRESSION position stays a sanctioned typed hole | name the missing value with a lambda: `(x) => add(x, 10)` |
| E047 | Invalid escape in a string literal — an escape Almide does not define (`"\q"`), or a `\u{…}` outside the Unicode scalar range (`"\u{110000}"`, surrogates). Both used to pass through SILENTLY as their own spelling (#1264) | Double the backslash for a literal one (`"\\d+"`), or use a raw string (`r"\d+"`); for a codepoint stay within U+0000..U+D7FF / U+E000..U+10FFFF (`"\u{0}"`, not `"\0"`) |
| E048 | A constructor pattern the SUBJECT does not have: wrong family (`some`/`none` destructure an Option, `ok`/`err` a Result, and the two never mix — `list.get`/`map.get`/`string.find` return `T?`, `int.parse`/`fs.read_text`/`json.parse` return a Result), a builtin carrier aimed at a USER variant, or a user case borrowed from another variant. The checker only rejected a ctor pattern over a plain SCALAR, so these bound their payload Unknown and died at build — a compiler-blaming banner, or invalid generated Rust for the foreign-case cell (#1341) | Use the subject's own cases; for the family swap the error's `try:` names the same arm position (`ok(..)`→`some(..)`, `err(..)`→`none`, `some(..)`→`ok(..)`, `none`→`err(..)`), and for a variant the hint lists its cases |
| E049 | `let ... in <expr>` is OCaml/Haskell syntax — Almide has no `in` keyword: bindings chain by newline and the block's trailing expression is its value | delete the `in`; what follows it is already the continuation. The fix-it is machine-applicable, so `almide fix <file>` removes every one mechanically |
| E050 | A local `fn` collides with a selectively-imported name (`import json.{parse}` + `fn parse`) — one bare name, two resolutions: the checker used to pick the local fn while lowering picked the import, so a call type-checked against one function and EXECUTED the other (#1425) | Rename the local fn, or drop the name from the import list and call it module-qualified (`json.parse`) |
| E051 | A file's `@dialect(N)` stamp names a HIGHER dialect epoch than the compiler implements — the file was verified against a newer language than the one being asked to compile it, so a success here would be luck rather than evidence | Upgrade the compiler; or, if the file really targets this dialect, run `almide check <file> --stamp` on a clean check to write the correct epoch (it only ever moves the stamp forward) |
| E052 | A call names a `@deprecated` function. The hint names the replacement and classifies the edit by COMPARING the two signatures: identical means the rename is the whole edit, anything else means the arguments need looking at | Same signature: `almide fix <file>` applies it unattended. Different signature: the hint still names the replacement, but the edit is yours — the auto-fix is withheld on purpose rather than risk a miscompile |
| E053 | An attribute name the compiler does not read (`@deprecatd`, `@inline`, anything invented). It parses and then nothing happens — before this warning a misspelled `@deprecated` left every caller unwarned while the author believed otherwise | Fix the spelling (the hint suggests the nearest real one, or lists the whole vocabulary). Almide reads: @extern @export @intrinsic @wasm_intrinsic @inline_rust @mutating @consume @borrow_ref @pure @schedule @location @derived @main @deprecated @dialect |
| E054 | `almide fmt` refused to write: formatting would not conserve the program (parse, AST, or comments — the #1309 `--safe` verifier). The file is left untouched | Nothing in your source — this is a FORMATTER bug; report the file, leave it unformatted, format the rest |
| E055 | `?.` on a Result — the optional chain is Option-only (`o?.f` is `option.map`) | Convert or unwrap first: `(r?)?.field` (Result→Option, then chain), `(r ?? fb).field`, or `match` |
| E056 | (warning) `?` on an Option is a no-op — the operand is already an Option, nothing converts | Drop the operator; to unwrap use `?? fallback`, `match`, or `!` (effect fn) |
| E057 | fn declaration has no body — only @extern/@intrinsic may omit it | Write `= expr` (or `= { ... }`) after the signature |
| E058 | Unhashable Map key: Float, Map, or a record/variant carrying one anywhere in its fields (a FUNCTION in the key is E016) | Key on String/Int/Bool (or a record/variant of those); carry the unhashable value on the VALUE side |
| E059 | `for` over a non-iterable head (`for x in 5`) — the loop head must be a List or a Map | Iterate a List, a range (`for i in 0...n`), or a Map (`for (k, v) in m`) |
| E060 | (warning) Import hygiene: a module imported and never used, or imported twice under two names | Remove the unused/duplicate import; `import _name` suppresses a deliberate one |
| E061 | Top-level `let` bound to a lambda — the closure has no home in a module constant and the binding is not callable | Declare it as a function: `fn name(…) = …`; a `let`-bound lambda inside a fn/test body is fine |
| E040 | Retired json.*/value.* alias — the dynamic surface has one name per operation: `value.*` is the data model, `json.*` the format (parse/stringify) | Use the named `value.*` survivor (`json.as_int(v)` → `value.as_int(v)?`, `json.get` → `value.field(v,k)?`, `value.get` → `value.field`), or run `almide fix <file>` |
| E420 | Function visibility violation (callee is private) | Make the callee public, or add a public shim |

A rustc 4-digit code (`error[E0XXX]`) leaking through always indicates
an Almide codegen bug, not a user error — report at the issues URL.

## Project layout

```
mypkg/
  almide.toml          # [package] name = "mypkg"
  src/
    main.almd          # entry: `import self.<sibling>`
    classifier.almd    # sibling module
```

Sibling import is `import self.classifier` — no file paths.

## What Almide is NOT

- Not Haskell/ML — no `let rec`, no `let … in`, no type classes (protocols exist but have explicit `impl`), no HKTs.
- Not Rust — no lifetimes, no borrow checker surface syntax, no `unsafe`, no traits-as-data-attributes.
- Not JS/Python — no dynamic typing, no `null`, no exceptions, no method-call syntax (`x.foo()` on non-UDTs).

Cross-language idioms that compile in other languages and break here:
`let x = … in body` (OCaml), `head :: tail` (Haskell), `[a, ...rest]`
(JS/Rust), `int.gt(a, b)` (Go-ish), `x.toUpperCase()` (JS method chain).
Diagnostics for each carry a `try:` snippet that shows the Almide form.

## For agents and harnesses

- Start by calling `almide ide stdlib-snapshot` once and embedding the
  result in your SYSTEM_PROMPT. It is the authoritative inventory
  (~3.5K tokens text, ~14K JSON).
- On compile error, read the `hint:` and `try:` sections of the
  diagnostic — they are designed to be copy-pasteable.
- Do not write `test "…" { }` blocks in harness-submitted code unless
  the harness explicitly asks for them; this is the top parser cascade
  cause.

## Meta

- License: MIT or Apache-2.0 (see LICENSE files).
- Repo: <https://github.com/almide/almide>
- Dojo (MSR benchmark): <https://github.com/almide/almide-dojo>
- Current stable: v0.59.1 (prev v0.59.0). v0.59.1 is the CHECK-GREEN-MUST-BUILD release: a layered DDD verification (domain/application/infra packages over protocol ports, two structurally different adapters behind one generic use case) surfaced a batch of check-green/build-dead defects, all fixed with two-leg regression pins. (a) Cross-module convention methods carry their receiver BORROW MODE (#1549, incl. the mut-receiver emit-key mirror), a whole-parameter assignment to a `mut` param writes back through the &mut binding (#1550), and a protocol-bound generic's `mut` param keeps its by-reference convention through monomorphization (#1551) — the batch also covered derived-variant `.repr()`, top-level lambda `let` (E061), the Never guard else, guard-let in loops, and the mono/cross-module mut conventions. (b) A generic fn calling ANOTHER MODULE's generic fn monomorphizes the callee (#1556): the module-generic mono defers its prune, runs a second round after the top-level fixed point (module chains converge; BARE sibling spellings are discovered and rewritten module-scoped), and dedups instances against the module's own fn list — check was green while native died E0425 and wasm walled unlinked. (c) The C-132 move-mode bare-name landmine is defused (#1558): ambiguity is judged PER SCOPE, so a user `fn replace` no longer silently loses its write-back rewrite to stdlib's unrelated `string.replace` (the wall message had never named the collision). (d) A borrowed-param RHS stored into a field or indexed slot owns its String (#1560 — `t.name = s` emitted `&str` where the slot needs owned). (e) `almide fmt` keeps a protocol's `mut self: Self` (#1559 — the AST-conservation verifier caught the dropped `is_mut`). The pin doctrine these landed under is now recorded in-tree: a NATIVE codegen fix pins as a compiler test (tests/native_mut_param_pins_test.rs, 5 tests, A/B-verified red on the pre-fix compiler) because a wasm-leg corpus fixture never executes the broken native emit; the wasm-leg fixtures pin the cross-target behavior beside them. wasm subset: the COMPILER_FRONTIER debt reached ZERO — #1547's three shapes all lower (a `Result[(V1, V2), String]` transition return rides a generated `$__drop_vp_<A>_<B>` wrapper; closures CAPTURE rich lists — `List[<variant>]`/`List[<record>]` — through a tagged env class freed by a generated `__drop_env_rich` dispatcher; both port/adapter shapes run byte-identical under a 4 MB heap-cap churn), record-valued maps gained their stdlib family + the ROUTED shared-cell class (#1143 — `map.new/set/get` on `Map[String, <record>]`, a captured-and-mutated map cell frees through its type-specific sweep; C-319's statement widened), Codec `List[scalar]` defaults decode on wasm (#1520/#1563 — the `__decode_default_list_*` twins), and `mut` receivers/params lower via a borrowed-param COW admission (#1557 leg 1 — Dup+MakeUnique, no rc undercount, alias-exact). Record-pair Result returns lower (#1564 — `fn advance(s: St) -> (St, Ev)!` with St a RECORD, the transition shape over an ordinary aggregate: the `$__drop_vp_<A>_<B>` slot classification widened from variants to records — recursive-drop records recurse via `$__drop_<R>`, all-scalar records free flat — covering the (record, variant)/(record, record)/(record, String)/flat-record cells byte-identical and leak-free under heap-cap churn). The #1527 fuzz-frequency wall burn-down took the authoritative shard from 86 to 75 walls (result.filter's payload-independent `_h` twin with the interpreter VOTING via a new hof glue; list-of-maps and flat-payload-Result call arguments materialize as borrow views; `unwrap_or` results carry their read shape — the specimen fixture records that the trigger is the OPTION-RESULT nesting). Runtime: the HTTP client read timeout is CONFIGURABLE — `ALMIDE_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECS`, `0` = block until the server answers (a local-LLM endpoint needs 30-120 s before the first byte, #1561) — and the timeout error names the knob instead of the raw errno. Also: module-level String constants fold through const references (#1552), a `_`-named module's derived Codec decode links (#1555), and an oversized wasm fn is survivable — a >50k-locals fn walls WITH its name and count, and the local-slot reuse pass takes a 15,021-local render fn to 24 declared locals (#1554). Contracts 302, cross-target fixtures 592 -> 600 (all 3-way voting), walled-real baseline EMPTY, rustc-warning ratchet 0. Known frontier: #1557 legs 2/3 (cross-module protocol-method linking — the obvious resolution fix produces a silent-empty run, scouted with findings recorded on the issue; nested package imports); #1564's second repro family (`-> T?!`) still walls honestly, and the axis is MEASURED as the Ok payload's PRODUCER, not its type: a plain-constructor payload (`ok(some(Row { .. }))`) lowers for record and variant alike; an inline `ok(<stdlib call>)` payload (`ok(list.get(xs, 0))`, `ok(xs |> list.find(lambda))`) walls for BOTH kinds; the bare-call `if`-tail under the `?!` lift (`if b then list.get(xs, 0) else none`) walls for a RECORD payload while the same call's variant payload lowers — the last open #1564 cell; and binding the call first (`let hit = list.get(xs, 0)` then `ok(hit)`) lowers everywhere, the in-language workaround.
- Previous: v0.59.0 (prev v0.58.0). v0.59.0 unblocks protocol-based static DI: an effect protocol method reached through a generic bound now type-checks AND lowers. Two independent defects had made the shape unwritable, and neither was reachable without a bound. (a) The checker never applied the effect-fn Result lift on that path — `finalize_call_return_ty` gates the lift on `env.functions` carrying the callee, and a bounded call has no such entry while the receiver is still a type var, so `check` saw the bare declared `T` while codegen emitted a call returning `Result[T, String]`. The two agreed only while the value was passed straight through: returning it unchanged worked, binding it with `let` or using it as a `match` subject emitted invalid Rust, and a `!` was rejected outright (E034 on a scalar/heap return, E001 one level too deep on an Option return) or ICE'd in ConcretizeTypes with unresolved types. There was no spelling that both type-checked and lowered once the value was consumed — which is every repository, since one whose result is never read is not a repository (#1545). (b) mono's `fix_body_match_ty` overwrote `body.ty` with the declared `ret_ty`. An effect fn's body is not Ok-lifted until ResultPropagation, which runs downstream of mono, so a body typed as the Ok payload was CORRECT there, not stale; overwriting it made the body CLAIM to be a Result it never wrapped, and ResultPropagation's "already Result — nothing to repair" gate then skipped the lift, emitting a bare `()` where `Result<(), String>` was expected. Only programs carrying a generic bound were affected, because mono is what runs at all; the workaround was a trailing explicit `ok(())` (#1546). Pure protocol bounds were never affected — the basic form, `List[T]`, multiple bounds `[T: P + Q]`, and heap-returning methods all ran throughout, which is what isolated both defects to the effect path. The regression tests split by target on purpose: the checker lift is a corpus test (`spec/lang/protocol_generics_test.almd`, on the wasm leg), the ok-lift is a compiler test (`tests/effect_tail_generic_bound_test.rs`) because `wrap_non_result` is `matches!(target, Target::Rust)` and a corpus file would assert nothing on the wasm leg — the same reasoning as the #1210 tests. Known frontier: a `Result[tuple]` return still walls honestly on wasm (#1547) — `-> (St, Ev)!` declines while the same function over a record (`-> Outcome!`) lowers, which is exactly what an aggregate transition returning `(new_state, event)` hits.

- Previous: v0.57.1 (prev v0.57.0). v0.57.1 is a CORRECTNESS + ASSURANCE release; no surface changes, no breaking changes — everything 0.57.0 ran, 0.57.1 runs, including multi-GiB allocations on both targets. The integer-domain sweep: a new instrument (tools/domain_edge_matrix.py) crossed every public stdlib fn taking an Int with a fixed edge set on both targets and found 218 divergent cells, all closed, reducing to three mechanisms: (a) ADDITIVE bounds guards (`pos + len > blen`) defeated by their own arithmetic under wrapping Int — worst case `bytes.read_string_at(b, -1, 3)` returned the heap block's cap field AS STRING CONTENT, exit 0, both legs; every guard is now subtractive (C-054); (b) UNSIGNED steps inside signed arithmetic, native only — datetime.from_parts wrapped negative months, math.choose accumulated in u64, string.from_codepoint turned 2^32 into a valid NUL codepoint, datetime.to_iso wrote non-UTF-8 bytes for out-of-range years; all match the always-i64 self-host now; (c) RAW failure forms — list.range(i64::MIN, 3) was a native capacity-overflow panic (exit 101); every allocating path now fails through checked arithmetic + try_reserve into the single defined `Error: out of memory` + exit 1 on both targets. A unified 2 GiB allocation ceiling was implemented mid-cycle and WITHDRAWN before release (ratified ○×: A) after a nine-compiler survey found zero precedent for a chosen cross-target cap — each leg allocates to its own structural bound, and native satisfying what wasm32 cannot is the contracted divergence C-197 declares, per-cell in proofs/domain-edges.toml (64 declared, 0 untriaged). Also: io.read_n_bytes(i64::MAX) read NOTHING on wasm (i32 truncation at the host floor) — now chunked 64 MiB reads with no cap on the answer; bytes.chunks no longer computes its count from an overflowed `(total + size - 1)`. Fixed, all live in 0.56.0: (a) COMPILER PANIC — `guard let` inside a for/while body crashed lowering (#1204; the loop form was the construct's most natural use and had zero coverage — C-224 now pins 12 byte-identical shapes); (b) `Bytes?`/`Matrix?` `??` inline in a call argument emitted invalid Rust (#1210, E0308 — the RcCow arm mismatch; found by the bytes semantics-manifest measurement on its first run); (c) matrix transcendentals diverged native ⇄ wasm and BY HOST ARCH — up to four answers for one program (#1197; pow/rope/sigmoid now route the vendored musl-libm, softmax/gelu run ONE canonical unfused fast-exp on both legs — wasm has no FMA instruction, so unfused is the only reachable fixed point; C-223); (d) an expression-nested `!` on wasm read the err block's payload slot as the value (#1183, accept-and-wrong — ANF-hoisted to the proven bind-position machinery; C-222); (e) the certificate-layer itoa printed negative i64 as u64 (sign + wrap-negation magnitude, i64::MIN exact). - Previous: v0.56.0 (prev v0.55.0). v0.56.0 removes the `list.try_*` family — the ADR-0006 arc's final act, one release after its deprecation window. SURFACE CHANGE: the seven twins (`try_map` / `try_filter` / `try_flat_map` / `try_filter_map` / `try_fold` / `try_find` / `try_each`) are gone as public names; a call is E043 carrying the mechanical rewrite (`list.try_map(xs, f)` → `list.map(xs, (x) => f(x)!)!` — fold takes the two-arg lambda, the rest are the same shape). The MEANING lives on the fallibility-polymorphic core (v0.55.0, D1): the callback's `!` is the strategy, one name per combinator — `try` was a loan-word whose lenders disagree (Rust try_fold = short-circuit, Swift/Zig try = propagation = almide's `!`), and the ambiguity retires with the name. Mechanics: the seven bodies persist as `__fallible_*` INTERNAL CARRIERS the checker's fallible-callback normalization routes to (named `__try_*` for one release; naming one in source is now the same E043, because deleting the public spelling while the carrier stayed writable — and IDE-visible — renamed the second spelling rather than removing it), so the polymorphic form's behavior — and its wasm closure-lifting native-fallback frontier, ledgered since 0.53.6 — is the same shipped code; the family gate completes its three-state arc (completeness matrix 0.53.6 → frozen seven 0.54.0 → EMPTY surface + carriers-exist now); the one real-world use (tools/almide-gates, the measured migration cost of the whole removal) moved to the polymorphic spelling.
- Previous: v0.55.0 (prev v0.54.0). v0.55.0 is the EXPLICIT-PROPAGATION SWITCH: the 0.54 deprecation window closes and the ADR-0008 world is the only world. (a) Implicit propagation (auto-?) is REMOVED — every formerly-stripping position (statement, un-annotated let/var, condition, value-pattern match subject, interpolation, assignment) is the hard error E041 with the mechanical `!` insertion; a discarded statement-position Result is E042 (must-use, EVERY fn kind) with the two escapes spelled in the hint (`expr!` propagates, `let _ = expr` discards); `let _ = f()` now genuinely DISCARDS — the err does not propagate (pre-switch it did; C-217 pins the new behavior cross-target). The two hazards the implicit form carried — pattern-shape-dependent stripping and annotation-inverted behavior — are structurally gone (spec/lang/explicit_propagation_test.almd fails on 0.54 by design: the A/B). (b) The fallibility axis reaches fn types (ADR-0006 D1, #1108 Phase 2a): the core list HOFs are 1-bit fallibility-polymorphic — `list.map(xs, (x) => f(x)!)!` (or a named `-> T!` callback) instantiates the first-err short-circuit form; one name per combinator, the callback's `!` carries the strategy (Swift SE-0413's shape, E=String per ADR-0002). Consequently `list.try_*` is DEPRECATED (E043, the hint IS the mechanical rewrite) and the seven are removed together in v0.56.0. (c) `result.collect`/`collect_map` are REMOVED (ADR-0007's window): partition is the substance, the polymorphic map the first-err traversal; the List[String]-err join on `!` outlives the retired name (spec/stdlib/result_errjoin_effect_test.almd). (d) `T?` is general Option shorthand (ADR-0010): valid in EVERY type position, atom-tight binding (`(A) -> B?` returns Option; `((A) -> B)?` is an optional fn value — measured 0 uses; nested spells `(T?)?`), and CANONICAL — `almide fmt` normalizes `Option[T]` to it (spec+examples migrated, 1044 sites; stdlib keeps longhand as the boundary-unification witness). (e) #1125 is fixed (C-216): explicit `!` on a declared-Option effect call was the wasm silent-wrong class (raw Option block read as a Result — hit=999 then an rc_dec trap, pre-existing since 0.53.6); the spelled marker is now the implicit strip's identical twin on native, wasm, AND the interpreter (the 3-way oracle dissented until the strip landed there too) — the drop-in equivalence the switch REQUIRES. Output-parity ratchet 406 → 408; contracts 215 → 217.

(a) The pure-fallible return marker `-> T!` (#1103 Phase 1, ADR-0002): `fn parse(s: String) -> Int!` is `Result[Int, String]` without the effect axis — parses in return position, resolves through the checker, round-trips `almide fmt`; the value-tail lift is Phase 1b. (d) `result.collect`/`collect_map` are deprecated (E039, ADR-0007): Rust's collect short-circuits where almide's collected ALL errors — an opposite strategy under the same name loses the writability tiebreak; `result.partition` is the substance. (e) Error-doctrine lints (ADR-0004): E035 flags branching on error TEXT, E036 flags a `map_err` that drops its error argument (`(_)` is the intentional discard). Checker holes closed (#1115–#1121): E037 same-head eq mismatches, E038 line-crossing `??`, guard-else exit const-folding with new signed comparison folds, the `??` fallback constraint, Result[Unit] interpolation. (g) Stdlib per ADR-0004 D4: the fs content-reader `*_if_exists` family (absence-as-Option with runtime NotFound classification, C-215); `assert_none`/`assert_err` complete both assertion polarities; `option.to_result` generalizes over E with a pure bundled body. docs/specs/result-option-effect.md is REWRITTEN from 287 measured probe cells and the native⇄wasm output-parity ratchet rises 383 → 406.
- Previous: v0.53.6 (prev v0.53.5). v0.53.6 is the ZERO-COMMITTED-SHELL unblocker: the two primitives whose absence forced real programs back to `var + for` and `perl -e 'alarm'`. (a) The `list.try_*` family (#1041) — `try_map` / `try_filter` / `try_flat_map` / `try_filter_map` / `try_fold` / `try_find` / `try_each`, each the core combinator with its callback lifted to `-> Result[_, E]`, short-circuiting on the FIRST err (later elements are never evaluated), so an effectful pipeline stays a combinator chain: `files |> list.try_map((f) => read_meta(f))!`. (b) `process.exec_status_timeout(cmd, args, timeout_ms)` (#1040, C-214) — the ONE admissible timeout: spawning a process is already outside the byte-identity contract, so bounding it adds no nondeterminism (bounding a pure computation would — the 0.29.0 removal stands; today's `fan.timeout` is the separate deterministic omega-replay form). If the deadline fires the child is KILLED and the err is exactly `exec timed out after <ms>ms`; whether it fires belongs to the host. Chatty children cannot deadlock the drain (reader threads); the parity gate dropped its perl `alarm; exec` wrapper for it.

- Previous: v0.53.4 (prev v0.53.3). v0.53.4 is a WRITABILITY patch — four defects a writer hits and one idiom that no longer needs a workaround. (a) A tuple pattern in LAMBDA parameter position now binds every name (#1060): the parser had produced `tuple_names` since the form existed but nothing downstream read it, so the second name was undefined and the writer got E003 on a variable they had just written. `((k, v)) => …` works on `map.entries`, `list.enumerate` and any pair list, so CLAUDE.md's documented `let (a, b) = entry` rewrite is retired. (d) #1056 (false unused-variable warning on a directly-called lambda binding) was already fixed upstream and is verified closed.

- Previous: v0.53.0 (prev v0.52.0). v0.53.0 is the PLATFORM-CONFORMANCE release (the Wasm 3.0 / WASI audit burn-down): NaN observation is canonical on every target and host architecture (C-210 — the deterministic-profile stance applied at the language layer, with a machine gate pinning no-relaxed-SIMD/atomics/shared in emitted modules); the self-host linker walls same-name/different-signature collisions instead of emitting an invalid module (#1068); function-tail closure calls emit return_call_indirect (C-178); and the wasm leg now RUNS ON WINDOWS HOSTS with a per-push CI parity gate (#1066) — the fs path contract is recorded against what Go, Rust, and wasi-libc actually do on wasip1.
- Previous: v0.52.0 (prev v0.51.0). v0.52.0 is the JSON-INTEROP DECISION release: #1062 ("interop with the world's JSON is an accident, not a decision") is decided and closed with ZERO added mechanisms — no rename knob, no variant-tagging knob, no new syntax. The stance, now official in CHEATSHEET's "JSON & the wire" section: wire types mirror the wire's names verbatim (`traceId: String` in a wire type is correct practice, not a style violation — renamed-by-convention knobs are the one design whose failure mode is runtime-silent, which loses the MSR tiebreak); `as "wire"` is scoped down to keys that cannot be Almide identifiers; foreign tag shapes (internally-tagged unions) are hand-written codecs — per-case Codec records plus a ~1-line-per-case dispatch that composes with every derived Codec automatically. The semantics under that stance are C-209: derived Codec encode OMITS a none Option field (proto3-style unset; every peer that started null-by-default — serde, Go, aeson — grew an opt-out later, so Almide omits from day one), decode keeps folding missing/null to none, so decode(encode(x)) == x while encode(decode(doc)) normalizes; defaults stay emitted; a proto3 oneof is now just an all-Option mirror type with `= none` defaults — one key on the wire, zero special casing (the OTel demo's Jaeger-400 class dies at the root). `Value` fields pass through verbatim in both directions, making `Option[Value]` the sanctioned 3-state escape hatch (missing → none, explicit null → some(null) — the ONE Option cell where absent and null differ, RFC-7386-shaped). The #1061 class ("check passes, generated Rust fails") turned out to be 13 field-type cells wide, not 2, and is GONE both ways: Value/Option[Value]/List[Value]/Option[List] lower correctly, containers nest arbitrarily (#1065 — List[Option[T]] with meaningful element nulls, List[List[T]], Option[List[Option[...]]], via per-type recursive workers with Try only in bind position), and everything outside the closed grammar rejects at declaration with targeted E023 hints (Option[Option] at any depth is void on the wire; element-position Option[Value] has no absent state; sized numerics/Bytes/tuples/fn/Result are not wire concepts). The executable spec is spec/stdlib/codec_field_matrix_test.almd (every accepted cell's wire bytes + decode states + the retraction law) plus spec/wasm_cross/codec_none_omission.almd (byte-identical native == wasm) plus tests/diagnostics/e023-codec-* (every rejected cell). Cross-target reach (#1064): an Option block IS a 0-or-1-element list block, so both drop generators now normalize Option[heap] fields to their List twins before classification — variant record-ctors and records with Option[String]/Option[variant] fields lower on the wasm leg (previously an honest wall in call-arg position, and a LIVE LEAK for a record field holding a Var-built Option[String], whose some-payload a flat rc_dec never freed); some/ok over a list payload routes through the same ANF-materialize-retry the Call class uses; Option-field variant encodes ride per-case payload workers so the derived encode stays in the return-match subset. Two latent deriver bugs fixed en route: field bind vars were `_{name}`, so a Codec field literally named `v` (or a variant payload field named `tag`/`payload`) shadowed the document in emitted native Rust and mis-decoded at runtime ("expected Object") — binds are `_f_`-prefixed now; and CHEATSHEET documented a `{"tag","value"}` variant wire shape that has not existed for months (the derived form is externally tagged — `{"Click": [10, 20]}` — which is where #1062's own premise came from). The walled-real frontier is enumerated honestly: six functions in the new matrix file (the Result[List[Option[T]], String] heap-result arm class + record binds whose Option payloads sit outside the drop-exact set) are ledgered in proofs/walled-real-baseline.txt as the next brick, running green on the native leg meanwhile. E022's lift (allow `!` propagation in pure Result-returning fns — the one gap every peer language with hand-written codecs has an answer to) is split to #1067.

- Previous: v0.37.0 (prev v0.36.0). v0.37.0 is a CORRECTNESS + REACH release: sixteen new behaviour contracts (C-175…C-190), the cross-module link path made sound, and the code-health campaign finished. Cross-target correctness: a scalar `if` ARM now executes its statement effects — a mutable-global write inside the ordinary early-return guard `if bytes.len(d) < 12 then 0 else { bytes.set_i32_le(g, …); … }` lowers instead of walling, and an outer-`var` reassignment inside an arm hits that var's STABLE local instead of a frame-local rebind, which was last-writer-wins and printed 1 where native printed 1001 (C-188, a silent wrong value); sized-integer `^` wraps at the declared width like `+`/`-`/`*` — it reached the lane as a `math.pow` CALL and bypassed the wrap in three places (C-180), and `^` is the same total exponentiation as `math.pow` (C-184); `UInt64` reaches its full declared domain with every observer reading the slot unsigned (C-179); the heap-element `chunk`/`windows` twins clamp negative counts like their Int siblings did — `windows(xs, i32::MIN)` computed ~2^31 windows and hung wasm against native's instant `[]` (C-054, found by differential fuzz); `fan.any` returns the first Ok in LIST order whatever position it is in, lowered as one first-ok chain instead of duplicating the continuation per level (C-185); a mutable-global projection read in a loop-body call argument reads the CURRENT slot every iteration — the hoist walker descended through loop bodies and froze one stale handle for the whole loop (C-177); an in-place mutator writing through a module-level `var` buffer COWs the SLOT (C-187, it blocked almide-graphics/nendo's VRM viewer, whose whole scratch arena is one module-level buffer); mutual tail recursion runs at unbounded depth via `return_call` (C-178); `args.positional` stops dropping the first argument (C-181); a negated float literal takes its context's float type so `Float32` negatives build (C-182). Lowering reach (each previously an honest wall): variant-typed List literals in bind and heap-result-if-arm position (C-175), `some`/`ok` around an inline tuple-returning call (C-176), a loop-carried append of list-of-scalar-records (C-183), an inline index read appended to a list accumulator (C-186), `bytes.data_ptr` self-hosted on wasm, `io.read_all` as a chunked stdin read-to-EOF loop, and main-less modules with `pub fn` exports rendering as LIBRARY wasm with a synthesized empty start. Cross-module linking was the release's deepest fix: module top-let ids are disambiguated across regions and remapped into a reserved band so two regions cannot collide, const-fold substitution is scoped per region (one module's literals could replace another region's same-numbered vars), the name bridge is keyed by the origin spelling both sides carry, and an in-place mutator receiver resolves LOCALLY before the globals map — `value_or_global` documents that precedence and the two are not one numbering space, so a sibling's first PARAMETER and a consumer's first top-let are both `VarId(0)`. The monomorphization key is now injective: it keeps EVERY bounded type variable (compound types returned no name and were silently dropped, so two instantiations shared one specialization) and gives tuple and function types real names. Instrument: the nightly fuzz builds in its own job so the campaign spends the whole runner lifetime fuzzing, with the budget sized to the lifetime the runner actually grants; the fuzzer's native leg is split into timed build and run steps so a slow rustc under load can no longer masquerade as a hang; and `almide build` stages and renames its output instead of copying onto the existing inode, which macOS's vnode signature cache turned into a SIGKILL on the next exec. Tooling: `almide fmt --check` is a REAL gate — it names each unformatted file and exits non-zero, and directory arguments recurse; previously it printed the formatted text and exited 0 unconditionally, so every CI gate written against it was a no-op (#919). The formatter also stopped emitting optional statement semicolons and a leading blank line — output that appears in no hand-written Almide anywhere in the repo. Chore/quality: the codopsy campaign (#851) is complete — all five target crates at or above grade, almide-mir 67 → 75 (B) with issues 384 → 276, achieved by classifying the 175 over-threshold functions first and extracting only the 62 that were genuinely complex (over BOTH thresholds); the 105 that were cyclomatic-only are flat dispatch tables where splitting makes the code worse. Every extraction is verified as a pure move by corpus certificates (5,365 functions × 5 artifacts) byte-identical against a same-HEAD baseline. Sequence-suffixed split files (`_p2`/`_b`/`_c`) are renamed to content names across codegen, frontend, interp, ir, tools, egg-lab and lsp; the workspace (not just the root package) now runs in CI cargo tests; and the embedded stdlib payload has a size ratchet. `env.os`/`env.temp_dir` are named and bounded as the equivalence law's ONLY exemption (C-189). The nightly differential fuzzer, running a full campaign again for the first time in weeks, then caught two defects that were fixed before this release shipped. One was a same-day regression: converting the MIR STRICT-value mode from a process-global flag to a scoped guard put the guard around the IR phase, but the mode is read by MIR op LOWERING, which runs after that guard drops — the old global was never reset, so lowering had been inheriting strict mode by leak. Every deferred `Op::Const` ZERO went back to rendering as an executable 0, and wasm printed 0 where native printed 100. The guard now spans the whole render and the lowering entry ASSERTS the mode, so the invariant is checked on every wasm render rather than by one test. The other was an acceptance gap with a wider hole than its repro: the declared-type context reached an int literal through exactly ONE level of unary minus, so `let m: Int8 = -(300)`, `--300` and `-(-300)` were never range-checked at all and rustc rejected the emitted `-300i8` after `check` accepted. The literal is now found through its whole paren/minus chain, and the NET sign decides — `-9223372036854775808` is `i64::MIN` and valid while `--9223372036854775808` is +2^63 and no signed type holds it. Underneath the first finding was a real wall, also closed here: a closure's env holds its non-heap captures in raw 64-bit slots, but the class test restated a SUBSET of `is_heap_ty`'s negation (`Int | Bool`), so a `Float` capture — and every sized int width — refused to lift and walled the ENCLOSING function. Float needed no reinterpret: a MIR float local already holds its bits in an i64 and the float ops reinterpret around themselves (C-190).

Docs: sixteen new stdlib pages — EVERY bundled module now has one (39/39, up from 23): `path`, `args`, `html`, `mem`, `net`, `zlib`, `base64`, `hex` plus the eight sized-numeric conversion modules, all carrying the machine-owned signature index, with executable worked examples — that is how three of the defects above were found. The module interface can also finally NAME the sized numerics (`Int8`…`UInt64`, `Float32`/`Float64` are their own `Ty` variants, not `Named`, so every signature involving them had serialized as `unknown` — `int.to_int8` read `(n: Int) -> ?`).
- Previous: v0.34.3 (prev v0.34.2). v0.34.3 retires the last known lifted-effect ABI hole (#841, the sibling v0.34.2's notes flagged): a CAN-ERR lifted effect fn (`effect fn -> T` whose body can propagate an err, `T` non-Result) compiled to a runtime HYBRID on the wasm leg — ok paths returned RAW `T` while `!`-propagation paths returned a wrapped Err block, two shapes no consumer can discriminate at runtime, so a first-class `Result[T, String]` use (the call passed as a Result argument) silently misread the raw payload and OOB-crashed in the caller's scope-end `__drop_result_value`. Pre-existing (reproduces on v0.33.6). The fix makes the callee ALWAYS wrap, by extending two existing mechanisms rather than adding new ones: (1) the AUTO_WRAP ABI registry now admits EVERY non-Unit can-err lifted fn — the old stmt/tail-position `!` heuristics were an approximation of "can this body err" and missed a branch-nested or argument-position `!`; `compute_can_err` is the precise predicate. Declared-Unit can-err fns are untouched: the Unit classification arm already treats `AUTO_WRAP ∪ can-err` uniformly (`wrap_unit_body_in_ok` — the generated `__almd_test_N` harness precedent, which is also why a naive first-class-use WALL regressed 44 spec files when tried and was abandoned). (2) The heap-result arm machinery's ok-payload wrapper — which the AUTO_WRAP `body.ty` override relies on to wrap each ok arm — was gated to `LitStr | Var | ConcatStr` arms and let CALL-shaped arms (`value.object(..)`, `value.int(n)`) through raw, the other half of the hybrid; `Call` joins the gate, and a `Result[Value, _]` wrapper now routes its drop through the recursive `DropResultValue` instead of the flat String path. A side effect worth naming: generated programs that previously WALLED at the hybrid boundary now lower and run — the differential fuzzer visibly slowed per program because it stopped skipping them, a coverage widening. Fixtures: `spec/lang/effect_result_arg_test.almd` grows the can-err ok/err first-class-argument shapes, all running via the wasm leg. Gates: 303-file spec corpus on both targets with zero regressions, 75 cargo-test suites, diff-fuzz 2×300, output-parity byte-identical counts, the org yaml suite green on both targets.
- Previous: v0.34.2 (prev v0.34.1). v0.34.2 fixes two long-standing wasm-leg correctness bugs, both pre-dating the v0.34.x performance arc (they reproduce on v0.33.6) and both surfaced by this session's deep-verification sweep — one by a generative `xtarget-fuzz` campaign, one by running the org yaml package's test suite on both targets. (1) **`$__drop_opt_str_int` injection is now TYPE-driven** (#840): the recursive drop routine for `Option[(String, <scalar>)]` was only injected when the program called `map.find` — the one producer known when the routine was added — but the drop ROUTER keys on the type, so a plain `some((s, x))` literal produced a routed call with no definition and the WAT failed to parse. The gate is now the exact same type predicate the three router sites use (`Option[Tuple[String, non-heap]]` anywhere in an expression, param, or return type), so the routine is emitted exactly when a drop can route to it. (2) **Never-err lifted effect calls re-wrap in call-argument positions**: a lifted `effect fn -> T` returns raw `T` on the v1 leg, and the never-err pre-pass rewrites its call type to raw `T` everywhere; the `rewrap_never_err_into_result_targets` repair pass rebuilt a real `ok(..)` for bind/assign/List/Tuple/Record targets but never covered a CALL ARGUMENT whose callee param declares `Result[T, String]` — so yaml's `unwrap(parse(text))` handed the callee a raw Value block that its match read as a Result, returning the payload TUPLE handle as the Value ("" instead of "Alice" on wasm, correct on native). The pass now takes the per-function declared-param-type map and re-wraps positionally. The org yaml package's full test suite is green on both targets with this fix. The remaining sibling — a CAN-ERR lifted call used as a first-class Result, whose ok-paths return raw `T` while propagation paths return a wrapped Err block (no sound runtime discrimination; misread + OOB in the scope-end drop) — is tracked as #841 with a minimal repro; a naive wall regresses the generated test-harness runners, so it needs an ABI-level fix. Regression fixtures for both fixes (plus region fixtures pinning frontier-grow-inside-region, float payloads through compact scalar slots, and free-list churn between windows) are in `spec/lang/`. Gates: the 303-file spec corpus on both targets, 75 cargo-test suites, diff-fuzz 2×300 across two seeds, output-parity with counts identical to the pre-fix baseline.
- Previous: v0.34.1 (prev v0.34.0). v0.34.1 closes the adversarial half of the wasm-beats-Rust claim: v0.34.0 beat DEFAULT single-threaded Rust-wasm on all four perf benchmarks; v0.34.1 beats Rust-wasm even when the Rust side is expert-tuned per benchmark (`unsafe get_unchecked` indexing, `-C target-feature=+simd128` auto-vectorization, arena allocation via `typed_arena`) — fannkuchredux 0.83×, nbody 0.82× (vs +simd128, no SIMD on the Almide side), spectralnorm 0.85×, binarytrees 0.94× (vs the arena idiom, from 2.6× behind at the start of the arc), geometric mean 0.86× tuned / 0.57× default, sizes unchanged at 2.8–4.7× smaller. Three levers, all render-side inside the verified envelope (MIR + Perceus certificates untouched, same trust position as v0.34.0's BCE): (1) **flexible f64 classification across call boundaries** — scalar args to `CallFn`/`Call`/`CallImport`/`CallIndirect` no longer POISON the f64-local classification of surrounding arithmetic; the value reinterprets ONCE at the call boundary instead of freezing whole loop bodies into i64 slots (nbody's 34-arg `energy()` call was pinning the entire advance chain; removing the pin took nbody from 0.206s to 0.155s, past auto-vectorized Rust without emitting a single SIMD instruction). (2) **region-specialized allocation** (`region_alloc.rs`, #838 stage 1) — the `consume(produce(scalars))` window (build a tree from scalars, fold it to a scalar, drop it) becomes a bump REGION: `RegionSave` packs `bump|freelist<<32` into one local and EMPTIES the free-list so `$alloc` degenerates to a pure frontier bump, `__rgn_` clones of the closed callee set drop their `Drop*`/rc traffic, and `RegionRestore` reclaims the whole object graph in one frontier reset; qualification is mechanical (closed `CallFn` closure, no host caps / imports / indirect calls / mutable-global slots / `MakeUnique`, window-local heap value proven by occurrence count) and failing it just keeps the normal path. All-const nullary-ctor blocks (`Leaf`) collapse to ONE per-region singleton passed to the clones as a trailing param. (3) **compact headerless block layout inside regions** (`region_compact.rs`, #838 stage 2) — inside a qualified clone family the variant blocks drop the rc/len/cap header AND the tag slot: `Node(Tree, Tree)` goes from 36 bytes to the same 8 bytes (`[left:i32][right:i32]`) the arena idiom gets, handle fields pack as raw 4-byte pointers, scalar fields as 8-aligned i64s, and the match's tag read becomes a `select` on POINTER IDENTITY against the per-region singleton (every region block is a distinct bump address, so identity IS the tag; the singleton itself is rebuilt as a zero-filled compact twin so even a pathological padded-field read agrees under both layouts); `$alloc`'s bump+grow tail is inlined verbatim at compact alloc sites (the free-list is empty by the region invariant, so the scan half is dead — worth as much as the layout itself at ~67M nodes per binarytrees run). Family qualification is all-or-nothing and mechanical: one const-shape `Alloc` form, every raw load/store address chases to `base + header + 8k` with slot kinds unified across all sites, construction stores exactly-once per slot, an escape audit on every chased address, singletons required to be the max-arity-padded all-zero image of a nullary ctor. The measured ceiling probe that motivated stage 2 is recorded in #838: hand-stripping header stores + the tag bounds check from the stage-1 clones moved binarytrees ~1% — the 4.5× footprint reduction was the whole gap. Validation: 75 cargo-test suites, 301-file spec corpus on both targets, 600 differential-fuzz programs across two seeds, output-parity with zero real regressions, N=20 scale run byte-identical to the arena Rust program. Closes #838.
- Previous: v0.34.0 (prev v0.33.6). v0.34.0 is the wasm-beats-Rust performance release: Almide-wasm now outruns equivalent single-threaded Rust (`-C opt-level=3 -C lto=fat -C codegen-units=1 -C panic=abort`, wasm32-wasip1, wasmtime 42) on every benchmark in the perf suite — fannkuchredux n=11 at 0.79×, nbody 5M at 0.92×, spectralnorm 5500 at 0.89×, binarytrees 18 at 0.61× Rust's time (geometric mean 0.79×, ~21% faster), with modules 2.8–4.7× smaller raw and 4.8–7.4× smaller when both sides get `wasm-opt -Oz`. Four levers, all inside the verified envelope (MIR + certificates untouched or provably preserved): (1) **bounds-check elision via guarded loop versioning** (`render_wasm_bce.rs`) — a hot loop renders twice behind a one-time entry guard that proves every elidable index stays in `[0, len)` for the whole run (up/down/two-variable induction bounds from the loop's own top-tested compare, plus constant indices; nested plans compose, with the induction argument restricted to root-depth positions so a nested increment can't outrun the outer break check); guard imprecision can only cost speed, never correctness — the slow arm is the byte-exact original. Rust-wasm keeps the equivalent slice checks where LLVM can't prove them away, which is where fannkuchredux flips from 1.48× slower to 21% faster. (2) **single-prim scalar wrapper inlining** (`scalar_call_inline.rs`) — a `CallFn` to a wrapper whose whole body is one pure-scalar prim (`math.sqrt` & co) is rewritten to the prim at the MIR level, which both removes the call and stops the call boundary from POISONING the f64-local classification of the surrounding arithmetic (one sqrt per iteration used to force the whole nbody advance chain back into i64 slots with reinterpret round-trips). (3) **the self-append rewrite** (`concat_to_append.rs` + a self-hosted `__list_append1` in `stdlib/list_concat.almd`) — `x = x + [e]` (also what `list.push` desugars to on the v1 leg) was a full-copy concat per append, O(n²) for every accumulator loop (spectralnorm's row build: ~4.8 GB of memcpy per run, whose cache pollution also slowed the inner loops); the exact five-op window now becomes one call that appends IN PLACE when `rc == 1 && len < cap` — the runtime rc check subsumes any static alias proof, so value semantics are preserved exactly (an aliased list still snapshots) — and grows by 2·len+8 otherwise. The certificate's loop-slot `(id)` stream is preserved verbatim; the first hand-written-WAT version of the runtime was correctly rejected by the runtime-growth ratchet (§4.1 — the hand-written WAT floor may only shrink) in CI, and the shipped version is self-hosted Almide. (4) **renderer peepholes**: `x*(x±1)/2 → shr_s 1` backed by a parity argument that survives two's-complement wrap (consecutive-integer products stay even mod 2^64; the two `i+j` materializations are matched by straight-line structural equality), and dead constant-store stripping. Two measured tradeoffs are documented rather than papered over: `wasm-opt -Oz` merges the versioned fast/slow copies back into one checked loop (~3× slower on spectralnorm — docs/wasm/WASM-OUTPUT.md now says to benchmark before applying it to compute kernels), and pow2 growth blocks measured ~10% slower than 2·len+8 on read-streamed vectors (block placement effects, noted in the source). Closes #826.
- Previous: v0.33.6 (prev v0.33.5). v0.33.6 is a large internal-quality patch: an AST-quality-driven (codopsy) decomposition pass across the whole codebase (root `src/` + every crate), bringing every one of the 16 codopsy-analyzed units from a 2026-07-11 baseline of 46/D (390 files, 3764 warnings) to C or better — root-src 93, almide-mir 67 (the hardest case, ten dedicated rounds against a scorer plateau — see below), almide-codegen 83, almide-frontend 79, almide-interp 75, almide-tools 73, almide-optimize 94, almide-dialect 77, almide-types 91, almide-syntax 87, almide-ir 82, almide-kernel 84, almide-base 88, almide-egg-lab 94, almide-lang and almide-perceus-belt already 100. ~460 commits, essentially all pure mechanical transforms — name-router/sequential-phase extraction, guard-clause flattening for max-depth, `unwrap()`→`expect()`/`?` for no-unwrap, dead-code removal, CLI output routed through shared `out`/`err` wrappers — each verified behavior-preserving via `classify_corpus` byte-identical certs against the pre-round baseline plus the full test gate (no observable behavior change on either target). Also fixed a real bug in the separate `codopsy` tool itself (github.com/O6lvl4/codopsy, released as v2.1.0): `score_complexity` always penalized at the hardcoded `cc>10`/`cog>15` defaults regardless of a project's configured `max-complexity`/`max-cognitive-complexity` (this repo's own `.codopsyrc.json` sets 20/30), so a relaxed threshold silently kept scoring at the tighter one — a whole band of complexity (cc 10-20 / cog 15-30) was invisible to the issue list yet still penalizing the score, which is why almide-mir's score plateaued for several rounds despite genuine issue-count reductions. Re-measuring under the fixed scorer afterward showed every crate's true score was already comfortably higher than the numbers above (mir 60→67, codegen 60→83, etc.) — this session's decomposition work remains a legitimate quality improvement, but the scorer bug, not remaining complexity, was most of what made the last few points of almide-mir's climb so hard. v0.33.5 fixes two bugs #828/#830 surfaced during v0.33.4's work. Bare `self` as a param only resolved inside `protocol { ... }` declarations — three independent sites re-resolved it from raw AST and needed the same `Self`→enclosing-type fix (`register_fn_sig`, `check_fn_decl`'s scope binding, `lower_fn`'s `IrParam.ty`); fixing all three then surfaced a codegen bug, where the parameter-list renderer escaped Rust keywords via a stale JS-era list (a `--target ts` leftover) instead of the canonical `is_rust_keyword` predicate, so `self` was never escaped — and raw-escaping (`r#self`) doesn't even work for `self`/`Self`/`super`/`crate` in Rust anyway (rustc: "self cannot be a raw identifier"). New `escape_rust_ident()` in `crates/almide-codegen/src/walker/mod.rs` is the actual single source of truth now: normal keywords go through `r#name`, `self`/`Self`/`super`/`crate` are renamed outright (`almide_self`, etc.), and all four emission sites (var reference, fn param, fn definition, fn call) route through it. Fixing the checker/lowering sites also exposed that `almide fmt` printed bare-self methods as the unparseable `self: Self` (the parser can never produce that text itself — bare `self` always consumes the whole param) — `fmt`'s idempotence gate (`fmt_roundtrip_idempotency_all_spec_files`) caught it on the new test fixtures; `is_bare_self_param()` in `crates/almide-tools/src/fmt.rs` now special-cases both param-rendering sites (plain `fn`, `protocol` method) to print bare `self` back out. `Fn(T) -> U` never parsed in any position because `parse_type_expr_inner` (`crates/almide-syntax/src/parser/types.rs`) checked for the lowercase `fn` keyword token, but the documented spelling is capitalized `Fn` — which lexes as `TypeName`, not `TokenType::Fn` — so it fell through to being misparsed as an inline variant constructor (`TypeName(Args)`) instead; fixed with a lookahead branch for `TypeName("Fn")` followed by `(`, reusing the same param-list-then-arrow parsing as the keyword path. New coverage: `spec/lang/bare_self_test.almd`, `spec/lang/fn_type_test.almd`. v0.33.4 removes `impl Protocol for Type { ... }` blocks from the language entirely (lexer/parser/AST/checker/lowering/formatter) — `docs/design/REJECTED_PATTERNS.md` had already rejected the pattern in favor of convention methods only (written the same day as the trait→protocol rename, `56e3b0ad`), but the parser/checker code was never actually removed and kept compiling for ~4 months undetected. `impl X for Y` now hits the keyword-typo hint system pointing at convention methods. The eager per-method signature validation that used to live in `register_impl_decl` (arity + parameter/return type checked against the protocol's declared signature, `Self`-substituted) is ported into `validate_protocol_impls`, so convention-style protocol methods are now checked at `almide check` time instead of silently passing and only failing later at native codegen (#829, closed); signature checking is skipped for generic implementing types for now, since nothing threads a type's own generic args back into the `Self` substitution yet (presence is still required), and `Ty` comparison strips module qualification (`m.Pigment` vs `Pigment`) so a cross-module Codec type doesn't false-positive. `spec/lang/impl_block_test.almd`/`impl_error_test.almd` are removed — every scenario they covered already had convention-style coverage elsewhere in `spec/lang/protocol_*.almd`. Also fixed: the parser's own top-level-declaration error message still listed `trait`/`impl` as valid tokens, and SPEC.md/CHEATSHEET.md documented `impl` as the preferred satisfaction mechanism, contradicting the rejected-pattern decision (#827, closed). Two still-open, unrelated protocol/type bugs surfaced during this work: a bare `self` parameter only resolves inside `protocol { ... }` declarations, not on any actual method (#828); `Fn(T) -> U` never parses as a parameter type, type-alias target, or return type in any position — use the bare-parens form `(T) -> U` instead (#830). v0.33.3 elides dead `Op::MakeUnique` copy-on-write guards for provably-unaliased locals (#824, `crates/almide-mir/src/alias_safety.rs`): `lower_place_mutation` previously inserted the COW/refcount check before EVERY in-place indexed write to a local heap value unconditionally, paying a runtime `rc > 1` branch even where the refcount can only ever be 1 — measurable in hot loops (fannkuchredux wasm: ~16% faster at n=11, 3.89s → 3.22s, byte-identical to native across n=7..12). A per-function LEAST-FIXPOINT dataflow pass proves which locals are never aliased (never a `Dup` src/dst, never a borrowed call argument to an opaque callee, never a `LoadHandle`-read record/container field, never flows out of a branch merge) and drops only the `MakeUnique` occurrences on those; `Op::MakeUnique`'s own semantics and rendering (the `CowSafety.v`-backed COW guard) are untouched. Landed in two commits after CI caught two real gaps this session's own local testing missed: `Op::Dup`'s `dst` (not just `src`) must be tainted — a module-global handle load + Dup can be aliased by another function's `let snap = g`, invisible to a same-function scan (`spec/wasm_cross/module_var_alias_cow.almd`, C-033); and `PrimKind::LoadHandle` (how record-field / heap-container-element reads are lowered — no dedicated "read field" op exists) must taint its `dst` unconditionally too, since a `Dup`'d value `Store`d into a container and later re-`LoadHandle`d back out gets a BRAND NEW `ValueId` with no recorded link to the original alias (`spec/lang/rccow_value_semantics_test.almd`'s "record copy shields the original's bytes field" — CI's `almide test spec/ --target wasm` caught this; the default `almide test`'s native auto-fallback for some files hid it locally). v0.33.2 fixes a silent-miscompilation class: `Parser::parse()` is a recovery parser — an unparseable top-level statement (never valid Almide grammar outside fn/effect fn/type/let/var/trait/impl/test) is dropped via `skip_to_next_decl()`, but `parse()` still returns `Ok` as long as some declaration survived, and several callers (almide-mir's `source_to_ir_with`, `almide compile`, `--target rust` emit, `almide fmt`'s default write-back) checked only the `Result` and never `Parser::errors` — worst case `almide fmt` could silently delete the dropped line from the file on disk. All four now check `.errors` and fail loudly (new regression test in almide-mir's pipeline.rs). The fix surfaced two more pre-existing bugs in cross-module drop-glue codegen (drop_sources.rs): the `__drop_opt_<R>` and `__krec_*` (map/set/list-uniq keyed-record normalization) generators used a module-qualified type name (`m.Cfg`) raw in a FUNCTION NAME position instead of sanitizing dots via `drop_fn_ident` — both fixed, closing the last eight `tests/crossmod_matrix_test.rs` red cells. Also removed the dead `--target ts/typescript` test runner (`cmd_test_ts`), a vestige of the March 2026 TS/JS codegen retirement that had degraded into writing Rust source to a `.ts` file and always failing with a deno/node parse error. This release was prompted by a live almide/playground production incident (`RuntimeError: unreachable` compiling the default sample) — root-caused separately to the playground's own `compile_to_wasm` still calling the RETIRED v0 wasm emitter (#782); fixed in the almide/playground repo to call `almide_mir::pipeline::try_render_wasm_source` (the same v1 entry the native CLI's `--target wasm` uses), redeployed and verified live. v0.33.1 is an internal-quality patch: five cognitive-complexity>100 functions across the MIR lowering and frontend checker are decomposed into named, independently testable helpers (list_call_name, try_lower_option_ctor, lower_expr, infer_expr_inner, infer_expr_inner_g2) — pure mechanical splits, no observable behavior change (verified via classify_corpus byte-identical certs over the full spec corpus, plus the full test gate). v0.33.0 is the wasm performance-parity + fuzz burn-down release: the five-rung renderer arc (#806, closed) takes spectralnorm from 17× to 1.9× vs native (nbody 1.4× — the SIMD-less floor; fannkuch 1.7×) via inline bounds checks, an IR-level pure-scalar inliner with a one-instruction `float.from_int`, f64-typed wasm locals (no reinterpret round-trips), direct-`br_if` loop conditions, and expression-tree fusion + constant-divisor strength reduction — modules also shrink 6-11%. The v1 test surface reaches ZERO: closure ignores 30→0 and the last crossmod KnownBroken cell opens (unannotated generic-ctor top-lets carry their solved payload type to every reader — checker post-solve write-back + v1-pipeline refresh + registration no-clobber, C-157). Fuzz taxonomy is rebuilt (honest subset walls are coverage data with a per-reason histogram, not findings) and eight divergence classes are fixed with contracts: ctor payloads never zero out (scalar-call/tuple/if-merged — C-158), `binary_search` duplicate-key index pinned to Rust std's branchless loop (C-159), json pretty escaping unified to the canonical 5-escape rule (C-095), negative `repeat` counts clamp to empty (C-054), and `to_fixed`'s decimals bound is made total at 0..=4096 (C-155). v0.32.0 was the differential-fuzz burn-down release (#796): silent-wrong-value and double-free families found by the cross-target fuzzer are fixed at the class level. The v0 wasm share family (`or_else`/`unwrap_or_else`/`unwrap_or`/`to_list`/`to_option`/`to_err_option`/`to_result`) now co-owns every kept payload (+1) — un-inc'd aliases double-freed at scope end after CORRECT output; the v1 leg gains the missing repr-routed twins (`option.or_else_h`, `list.slice_str`, the `sort_by` cached-keys desugar is gated to Int keys); the v1 TCO loop rewrite recognizes the auto-`?`-wrapped tail self-call (an err-capable effect fn's recursive arm previously compiled to "exit with the last base" — a carried accumulator returned its INITIAL value); `math.log/log2/log10(-0.0)` = -inf (the musl gate's sign-bit half was dropped); empty pad strings default to a space (native parity). Abort forms are normalized to ONE stderr line + exit 1 on both targets for assert (C-153), clamp (C-154), and to_fixed's decimals domain (C-155). The checker closes four acceptance-parity gaps (check accepted, native build failed): E024 extends to record fields and binop operands, E025 catches unresolved intermediate call slots, E029 rejects unknown type names, E030 rejects unorderable sort elements. `almide build` gains the content-addressed native binary cache (identical generated code from any path reuses one binary — warm builds ~0.06s), `almide fmt` escapes free-form strings (#797), and `almide test`'s wasm leg routes main+test files to the authoritative native fallback instead of silently running only main (#798).

- Previously v0.28.6 (prev v0.28.5). v0.28.6 crushes the two fatal wasm-parity bugs. (1) #696 — a loop rebuilding a list via `list.push` (dropped or swap-carried each round) trapped with a raw wasm OOB at n≳8000 while native merge-sorted 152k fine, and every such loop silently paid O(n²) bytes where it did not trap. Root cause was compound: LICM hoisted the loop-local `[]` allocation into a shared `__licm` temp (aliasing every iteration to ONE buffer, so per-iteration value semantics survived only via the COW guard), and the swap edge `cur = merged` marked the buffer although `merged` is DEAD after the swap — so the unconditional `__cow_check` re-cloned the whole container on EVERY push. Fixed statically, zero runtime change (contract C-131 / ALS-C5): LICM never hoists a heap-typed result out of a loop, and AliasCowPass elides a DIRECT whole-var alias edge whose source has no read or mutation after it (same-loop sources are re-declared before any use; a LIVE alias — source read after the copy — still clones, `alias_cow` / `bytes_set_value_semantics` byte-identical). Merge sort now byte-matches native at 152k in ~3s. Fixture spec/wasm_cross/loop_buffer_churn.almd. An earlier rc-gated `__cow_check_rc` attempt was REVERTED as unsound: `var b = a` carries no rc_inc for any type, so a refcount is not a sharing witness at bind granularity. (2) #705 — a `mut` parameter of a REALLOCATING container (List/String/Bytes) silently lost its writeback on wasm except for Unit-returning callees in statement position: `let i = push9(v, 7)` pushed into a discarded copy (wasm len=1 vs native len=3; an MLP printed loss 0.0). MutParamLoweringPass now lowers EVERY call position via a bottom-up IrMutVisitor — the call becomes `{ let (__mp_res, __mp_buf) = call; <writeback>; __mp_res }` (value callees return an (orig, buffer) tuple, destructured on the proven BindDestructure path; a hand-built TupleIndex read left the buffer dangling when the tuple temp dropped), writing back to bare vars (Assign) and record fields (`f(b.items, …)` → FieldAssign); bare-name collisions are excluded wholesale (the #692 class — rewriting callee but not caller is an invalid module). Contract C-132 / ALS-M13, fixture spec/wasm_cross/mut_heap_param.almd. Full bar: almide test 280/280 (267 wasm / 13 fallback baseline), wasm_cross release gate green, workspace green, frees-churn green, 132 contracts / 242 fixtures bidirectional.
